providers.title: Solvability and coefficient injectivity
providers.scope: A system over G is solvable in an overgroup exactly when the coefficient map G -> (G*F_n)/<<w_1, ..., w_m>> is injective. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Nonsingular systems are solvable (OpenAI)
providers.scope: For every group G and words w_1, ..., w_m in G*F_n whose exponent-sum matrix has rank m over Q, the coefficient map is injective; proved in lessons 2 to 5. Uses (UC), (KU), (INT) and (REL).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Kervaire-Laudenbach conjecture (OpenAI)
providers.scope: An equation in one unknown with nonzero exponent sum is solvable over every group. Uses Theorem 2.1.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Infinite nonsingular systems (OpenAI)
providers.scope: Any family of equations with linearly independent exponent rows is solvable over every group. Uses Theorem 2.1.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Primitive generators of the cohomology of U(d)
providers.scope: The exterior generators of H*(U(d); Q) can be chosen primitive, negated by inversion and compatible with all coordinate block inclusions. Uses (UC) and (KU).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Pullback along block-diagonal maps
providers.scope: For X -> diag(X_i^(s)) P the generator e_(a,d) pulls back to the sum over i with k_i >= a of the signed block counts times e^(i)_a. Uses (UC) and (KU).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Incidence manifolds are orientable
providers.scope: The manifold of pairs (W, E) of a unitary and an l-plane fixed by it is a compact orientable manifold of dimension d^2 - l^2. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Simultaneous fixed spaces (OpenAI)
providers.scope: If the signed block counts of unitary variables of sizes k_i form a matrix of full row rank, the variables can be chosen so that the fixed spaces of the block matrices diag(X_i^(s)) P_j have total dimension at least sum k_i. Uses (UC), (KU) and (INT).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Nested nonzero minors
providers.scope: A rational matrix of full row rank r has columns j_1, ..., j_r whose leading t x t minors are nonzero for all t. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The leading term of the incidence class
providers.scope: The dual class of the unitaries with an l-dimensional fixed space has leading term c e_(1,d) ... e_(l,d) with c nonzero. Uses (UC), (KU) and (INT).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The intersection number
providers.scope: The pullback of the product of incidence classes evaluates to a nonzero multiple of the product of nested minors. Uses (UC) and (KU).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The planar boundary obstruction (OpenAI)
providers.scope: On a connected disk-and-band surface in a sphere for a nonsingular system, if all boundary words but one are trivial, the last one is trivial. Uses (SURF), (UC), (KU) and (INT).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Counting disks and boundary circles
providers.scope: Row independence forces equally many positive and negative disks of each type, and a connected surface has 2 - 2K + b boundary circles. Uses (SURF).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The mixing involution
providers.scope: JSJ = S^-1, so SJ is a self-adjoint unitary of trace zero and l(SJ) = b/2. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The upper bound
providers.scope: For suitable X_i, J Theta fixes 2K directions and l(S Theta) <= 3b/2 - K. Uses (UC), (KU) and (INT).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Spaces for G and G*F_n
providers.scope: A presentation complex Y of G has fundamental group G, and its wedge with n circles has fundamental group G*F_n. Uses (PI1).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Piecewise affine circle coordinates
providers.scope: The n circle coordinates of a map of a punctured disk can be approximated within 1/12 by maps affine in lifts on one triangulation, with the same boundary behaviour. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Level arcs for several unknowns
providers.scope: Generic levels of the approximations consist of circles and arcs that pair the occurrences of each unknown with opposite signs, and levels of different unknowns are disjoint. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
